name: Greenpanel Industries Ltd
title: Greenpanel Industries Ltd - 542857 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 volume fell 3.4% YoY and consolidated EBITDA margin dropped to 7.5% from 9.6% as prices were cut; management says oversupply lasts two years, with 800,000-900,000 cbm of new capacity coming, though it also guides mid-teen MDF volume growth.

summary.headline: Greenpanel Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR407 crore, but consolidated operating EBITDA margin fell to 7.5% from 9.6% in Q1 on price cuts.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR407 crore, up 4.6% YoY and 16.4% QoQ, while total volume declined 3.4% YoY as OEM and export volumes lagged despite record retail MDF sales. Management cut prices to regain share after a steep Q1 price increase, which compressed ASPs by 6-7% QoQ and pushed consolidated operating EBITDA margin to 7.5%. Opening inventory carried from Q1 kept the benefit of the ~5% QoQ fall in cost of production out of Q2 results. Management guided to mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 and said H2 pickup is visible, though margin recovery depends on volume and chemical costs.

segments.name: Retail MDF and plywood
segments.commentary: Retail MDF sales in Q2 FY27 were the highest ever for the company in a single quarter, up 17% YoY; plywood sales rose 8.4% YoY. Management says retail earns more than OEM or export, with a margin differential of 5% to 20%.

segments.name: OEM (domestic converters)
segments.commentary: OEM was about 15% of domestic volume in H1 FY27, versus 25-30% a year earlier. Volume fell after the Q1 price increase removed OEM pricing benefits, and OEMs shifted to imports; management expects a return toward 20-25% share over time.

segments.name: Export MDF
segments.commentary: About 85% of exports go to the Middle East. Opening October export order book was about 13,000 cubic meters, but execution was constrained by container availability. Basic 18mm interior-grade export prices were about USD 200-220 per cubic meter FOB.

guidance_outlook: Targets mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 full year, with retail growing strongly and the H1 shortfall in OEM and export recovered in H2.
Aims for volume growth in line with the industry (15% and above) from Q3 or Q4 FY27; management said 'hope' rather than firm commitment.
Expects domestic MDF demand CAGR of 15-17% to continue, supported by the Furniture QCO 2025.
Expects chemical cost inflation to moderate in H2 FY27; raw material prices seen stable or slightly lower.
Management hopes MDF EBITDA margin can reach at least double digits in upcoming quarters; at 15% volume growth it said margins could reach early teens, not very high teens.
Targets net asset turn of 1.3x to 1.5x at capacity on a sustainable basis; no new capex currently in line.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is about 2,800-2,900 cubic meters per day, roughly 900,000 cubic meters per annum; Line 3 at Andhra Pradesh is already in operation, providing organic headroom.
No capex currently in line for the next few years, per the analyst's question and management's acknowledgement.
Industry capacity additions of about 800,000-900,000 cubic meters per year expected over the next 2 years.
Average industry utilisation estimated at about 70%; company's own utilisation was about 51% in Q1 and 55% in Q2 FY27.
Management indicated a new 250,000 cubic meter MDF plant costs about INR800-850 crore (per a peer's reported figure); a single larger line costs about 25-30% more than one half its size.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 price increase was about 15%, lifting domestic ASP 13.5% QoQ; Q2 saw price realignment and ASPs fell 6-7% QoQ as the company chose to be price-aggressive.
Export demand is intact: opening October export order book exceeded total Q2 export sales, but containers and vessel availability limited execution amid Middle East disruption and sea freight hikes.
Imports are no longer cheaper than domestic supply after freight and chemical cost increases.

Management expects oversupply for at least the next 2 years, with pricing pressure but a narrowing supply-demand gap; multi-daylight press capacity is becoming unviable and some smaller players are exiting or stopping production.
Competition in South India is rising with new plants from Action (first Gujarat plant commissioned in October 2026) and Rushil Decor; management says Action typically does not undercut.

qa_highlights.question: Why has OEM volume not recovered and will it improve in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 price increase removed OEM pricing benefits, and OEMs placed longer-term import orders that lingered into Q2. It hopes Q3 OEM volumes will be much better than Q2, with October moving in the right direction but not yet at expected levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% cost-of-production reduction reflect in margins in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said chemical prices are volatile and hard to predict. It said the Q2 margin hit came from opening inventory of about 50,000 cubic meters made at higher cost; higher utilisation would add operating leverage, and fixed cost per cubic meter has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: Why are realisations lower than smaller peers such as Greenply and Century?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its large OEM and interior mix lowers the value-added share of its average realisation. It claimed that on like-for-like products it is at par with Action, at a premium to Greenply and Century.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 OEM share and the expected H2 and FY28 share?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM was about 15% of domestic volume in H1 FY27, versus 25-30% last year. Management expects a return to 20-25% as retail grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export order value and H2 export expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an opening October export order book of about 13,000 cubic meters, valued at about USD 200-220 per cubic meter FOB for basic 18mm interior grade. Container availability was the main constraint on execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margins by business, and is double-digit MDF margin achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said retail makes more money, with a 5-20% margin differential, and gave no separate export EBITDA per cubic meter. Management said double-digit MDF margin is its aim and hope.

risks_watch: Pricing pressure and oversupply: about 800,000-900,000 cubic meters per year of new industry capacity over the next 2 years; Action's new Gujarat plant adds competition in South India.
OEM recovery: OEM share of about 15% has not recovered, and OEMs have shifted to imports.
Export execution risk from container and vessel shortages and freight volatility linked to the Middle East.
Margin recovery depends on chemical cost trends, which management calls unpredictable, and on whether the company's ~55% utilisation rises.
Management's FY27 volume target (mid-teen MDF growth) depends on H2 OEM and export recovery; watch Q3 FY27 volume growth versus the 15% industry-level target.
Margin gap versus Greenply: management attributes it to utilisation and value-added mix; Q1 MDF EBITDA was 10-10.5% for the company versus 7-8.5% for two other listed peers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the retail and QCO outlook, but cautious and sometimes evasive on margins, pricing and OEM timing. Management repeatedly used words such as 'hope' and 'aim' and declined to give export margin figures or a firm date for OEM recovery.
key_quotes: The retail MDF sales made during Q2FY27 were the highest ever for Greenpanel in a single quarter.
Price reduction with the cost of goods staying a bit elevated optically is what led to margin contraction in Q2FY27.
Operating leverage is playing out. If you look at our fixed cost per cubic meter, that has come down for sure, but it is not enough. We need to do more volume.
So it is a value accretive proposition and with the pricing where it is today, I think we are making sufficient amount of money there on export.

growth.why: Management targets mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 (aim, with H2 pickup 'hoped' for), backed by an export order book of about 13,000 cbm and retail growth of 17% YoY, but no new capacity or capex is in line and utilisation is only about 55%, so the backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin fell to 7.5% in Q2 from 9.6% in Q1, but a ~5% QoQ cost-of-production cut is not yet in P&L due to ~50,000 cbm of higher-cost opening inventory, and management hopes MDF margin reaches double digits, though it guided only to early teens at 15% volume growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 51% in Q1 and 55% in Q2 FY27 and management says no capex is in line for the next few years, with Line 3 in Andhra Pradesh already operating for organic headroom.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management aims for mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 and hopes for 15%+ growth from Q3 or Q4, but Q2 total volume fell 3.4% YoY, OEM share is down to about 15% from 25-30%, and the target is described as a hope rather than a firm commitment.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: With utilisation at about 55% and industry utilisation near 70% amid 800,000-900,000 cbm of new industry capacity, management has no capex in line and the call points against a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 ASPs fell 6-7% QoQ after price cuts, revenue grew only 4.6% YoY, and management expects oversupply for at least 2 years, so upward revision looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 mid-teen volume target depends on H2 OEM and export recovery, while Q2 volume fell 3.4% YoY, export execution was constrained by containers (13,000 cbm opening order book), and chemical costs are volatile.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed in the call.

rows.label: Export order book recovery to 13,000 cbm
rows.why: Opening October export order book was about 13,000 cbm (above Q2 export sales), but execution is limited by container and vessel availability amid Middle East disruption.

rows.label: Chemical cost easing and H2 cost benefit
rows.why: Management expects chemical cost inflation to moderate in H2 FY27 and a ~5% QoQ cost-of-production fall to flow through once 50,000 cbm of opening inventory is consumed, but calls chemical prices volatile and hard to predict.

rows.label: Further net debt reduction
rows.why: Net debt is INR133 crore and falling, working capital cycle improved 5 days vs 30 June 2026, and net asset turn target of 1.3-1.5x is set at capacity.

tone.note: Management was confident on retail demand (+17% YoY, record quarter) and the QCO outlook, but cautious and sometimes evasive on margins, pricing, OEM recovery timing and export margins, repeatedly using 'hope' and 'aim'; analysts pressed on the margin gap versus peers and OEM share loss.
